metadata.title: Trump's 2017 Tax Cuts Add $1.9 Trillion to Deficit — 83% of Benefits Go to Top 1%

existing_copy_for_context_only.short: Trump's 2017 Tax Cuts Add $1.9 Trillion to Deficit — 83% of Benefits Go to Top 1%
existing_copy_for_context_only.medium: The 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act signed by Trump on December 22, 2017, added an estimated $1.9 trillion to the federal deficit over 10 years according to the Congressional Budget Office. Analysis by the Tax Policy Center found that approximately 83% of the law's benefits flowed to the wealthiest 1% of Americans. The law slashed the corporate tax rate from 35% to 21% while providing comparatively modest relief to working and middle-class families. The deficit explosion it created set the stage for future fiscal crises.
existing_copy_for_context_only.long: President Donald Trump signed the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act on December 22, 2017. The law reduced the corporate tax rate from 35% to 21% and changed individual rates and deductions. The supplied Tax Policy Center support note says a later Congressional Budget Office estimate put the conventional deficit increase at nearly $1.9 trillion over fiscal years 2018–2027, before interest on the added debt. TPC’s distributional analysis projects that in 2027 the top 1% would receive about 83% of that year’s total tax benefit. That is a projection for one year, not the share across the law’s full lifespan, and it is separate from the deficit estimate. The focused request to the linked TPC briefing returned HTTP 403, so this account relies on the supplied source notes. Neither figure establishes that the deficit increase caused a future fiscal crisis; the populated medium’s final causal claim remains unsupported and needs correction or a specific source.
